title: Woobox Photo Contest vs Poll: Which Voting Format Is Your Entry In?
intent: A contestant searching how Woobox voting works, whether a Woobox poll is the same as a photo contest, or how supporters should find their entry.
angle: Explain from the entrant's perspective that a photo/video gallery may let people vote once for each submission, while a poll presents organizer-uploaded choices and can restrict a voter to one choice. Direct readers to verify the exact category, entry page, and contest rules before sharing a link.
overlap: Low. Platform-specific format intent; complement the broad photo-contest-votes article rather than repeat its promotion advice.

title: My Woobox Photo Contest Entry Is Missing from the Gallery: What Can I Check?
intent: An entrant looking for help because a submitted photo is not visible or cannot be found for voting.
angle: Give entrants a short check sequence: confirm the right contest/category and gallery dates, reopen the direct entry link, then ask the organizer whether submission approval is pending. Explain that only the organizer can approve or change campaign visibility.
overlap: High with existing /blog/contest-votes-not-showing/ and merged with the adjacent manual-approval brief below; reviewed separately, retain as a low-priority search-query variant that should redirect or be folded into one combined article.
status: merged-reviewed; combine with Woobox manual-approval brief; low priority

title: When Do Woobox Daily Votes Reset? Check the Contest's Time Zone
intent: A contestant or supporter searching when they can vote again in a Woobox daily-vote contest.
angle: Clarify that Woobox's documented daily-voting setting resets at 12 AM Pacific Time, while the contest's own eligibility rules and displayed deadline still control. Offer a simple note-taking method for the reset time and local equivalent; do not encourage repeat-vote workarounds.
overlap: Medium with /blog/daily-contest-voting/ and /blog/contest-voting-closes-today/. Keep this as a Woobox-specific timezone answer and link to the broader reminder guide.

title: Woobox Vote Limits Explained: Email, IP Address, and Facebook Login
intent: A contestant asking why supporters cannot vote, why a household appears to share a limit, or what one-vote-per-person means on Woobox.
angle: Translate the platform's documented restriction choices into plain language, including that IP limits can affect people sharing a home, school, or office network and Facebook-user limits require login/authorization. Center the entrant on checking organizer rules or contacting the contest owner; no bypass advice.
overlap: Medium with existing vote-troubleshooting and registration posts. Prioritize only if Search Console shows Woobox-specific queries; otherwise add as a section in the troubleshooting guide.

title: Woobox Vote Not Counted? What an Entrant Can Document for the Organizer
intent: A contestant asking why a Woobox vote did not appear or how to report a disputed count.
angle: Recommend recording the entry URL, category/round, time, displayed confirmation, and any relevant error, then asking the organizer to check its vote records. Explain that organizer exports may show blocked-vote indicators, but a shared IP can also be legitimate and a public count alone cannot identify voters.
overlap: High with /blog/contest-votes-not-showing/. Treat this as an expansion of that page unless Woobox-specific search demand justifies a standalone URL.
status: low-priority; preferred as a section in existing troubleshooting article

title: Why a Woobox Contest Asks Voters to Log In with Facebook
intent: A contestant or voter searching why a Woobox ballot requires Facebook login or authorization.
angle: Explain the documented connection between Facebook-user voting restrictions and login/authorization, and advise entrants to share the platform's actual voter steps before asking for support. Mention that organizers can choose different restrictions, but an entrant cannot change them.

title: Woobox Finalist Rounds: What a Vote Cap Means for Your Entry
intent: A contestant searching how Woobox vote caps, hidden entries, or finalist stages affect their chances and share link.
angle: Explain that organizers can set a maximum vote count and may hide an entry from the gallery until it reaches that threshold, while a unique submission URL can still allow voting. Tell entrants to confirm whether the cap is a qualifying threshold, a finalist rule, or a campaign-specific display choice.
